You who clarified the ultimate meaning of dependent origination, the intent of the Āryas,
And the profound, essential point of mere nominality and mere imputation,
Having departed to the state of supreme accomplishment,
To the feet of Buddhapālita, I pray!

The complete Pandita who established the system of tenets,
To the master Bhāvaviveka, I pray.

You clarified the philosophical systems of Vaibhāṣika, Sautrāntika, and Vijñānavāda;
Supreme among scholars, renowned as a second Buddha—
I pray to the feet of the master Vasubandhu.

To the feet of Kamalaśīla, I pray.

You who reveal the path of vast conduct,
To the one who, as prophesied by the Victor, opened the chariot-way of the Vijñaptimātra tradition,
To the feet of Asaṅga, I pray.

Through the power of reasoning based on the facts of the Buddha’s scriptures,
You opened wide a hundred gates of valid cognition to reveal the truth;
To the logician who grants the eye of discerning intelligence,
I pray to the feet of Dignāga.

translation:
In this way, regarding these profound and vast Dharma teachings well-explained by the Buddha, the Blessed One, those aforementioned masters of the noble land of India composed numerous marvelous treatises that open the wisdom-eye of beings endowed with analytical intelligence. Because these have existed without decline as texts for study, reflection, and meditation for nearly two thousand five hundred and fifty years until the present day, I have felt a desire to write this prayer of heartfelt reverence for those masters, remembering their kindness and aspiring to follow them with unwavering faith.

In this current era, when the world has reached a high level of development in science and material technology, and when there is great distraction and turmoil from the busyness of worldly life, it is of utmost importance that we followers of the Buddha gain faith in the Buddha’s teachings through understanding. Therefore, with an impartial mind, one should examine and analyze them thoroughly through the gateway of questioning to seek out the reasons. To generate faith accompanied by the companion of wisdom upon seeing those reasons, I recognized that these supreme, profound, and vast treatises—such as those by the renowned Six Ornaments and Two Supreme Ones, as well as Buddhapālita, Āryavimuktisena, and others—are indispensable.

Consequently, in addition to the long-standing tradition of painting the Six Ornaments and Two Supreme Ones, I have added nine other masters of the profound and vast lineages to create a new portrait of the seventeen panditas of Nālendrā. In connection with this, and prompted by the encouragement of some earnest Dharma friends, I have composed this "Prayer to the Seventeen Panditas of Glorious Nālendrā, Clarifying the Threefold Faith."

This was completed by the Śākya monk Tenzin Gyatso, who has attained a sincere and trusting faith in the excellent explanations of those masters and who sits at the end of the row of those studying their works. It was finished on the first day of the eleventh month of the Iron-Snake year of the seventeenth Tibetan sexagenary cycle—corresponding to December 15, 2001—which is 2545 years after the passing of the Teacher according to the Theravāda tradition. This was accomplished at Thekchen Chöling in Dharamsala, Kangra District, Himachal Pradesh, India. May it be virtuous.

translation: In this way, because the profound and vast Dharma teachings, which were excellently taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One, have been preserved without decline to this present day—nearly two thousand five hundred and fifty years later—through the marvelous and excellent explanations composed by the aforementioned masters of the noble land of India, who opened the eyes of wisdom for beings endowed with discernment, I have felt a desire to write this prayer of heartfelt reverence for those supreme scholars, both out of remembrance of their kindness and as a wish to follow them with unwavering faith; and, prompted by the encouragement of some earnest Dharma friends, in this current age where the world has reached a high level of development in science and material technology, and where there is great distraction and turmoil from the busyness of worldly life, it is of utmost importance that we followers of the Buddha gain faith in the Buddha's teachings through understanding, and thus, by examining and investigating thoroughly with an impartial mind and a spirit of inquiry, and by seeking reasons, to give rise to faith accompanied by the companion of wisdom, I have seen that these supreme and profound, vast treatises—such as the renowned Six Ornaments and Two Supreme Ones, as well as those by Buddhapālita, Āryavimuktisena, and others—are indispensable, and so, in addition to the existing tradition of painting the Six Ornaments and Two Supreme Ones, I have added nine other masters of the profound and vast lineage to complete the new creation of the painted images of the seventeen great scholars of Nālandā, and in connection with this, I, the Śākya monk Tenzin Gyatso, who have attained a sincere and unfeigned faith in the excellent explanations of those masters and who have taken my place in the ranks of those studying their excellent explanations, have completed this work, entitled "A Prayer to the Seventeen Great Scholars of Glorious Nālandā: Illuminating the Threefold Faith," at Thegchen Chöling in Dharamsala, Kangra District, Himachal Pradesh, India, on the first day of the eleventh month of the Iron Snake year of the seventeenth Tibetan sexagenary cycle, corresponding to December 15, 2001, which is 2545 years after the passing of the Teacher of the Theravāda tradition, may it be virtuous.
